title: "Reproduce the tutorial"
subtitle: "Requirements for reading, offline analysis and optional PyCPT fitting"

## Choose a starting point

This is a PyCPT tutorial. Reading either story or already-executed notebook needs
only a browser. Case one's default notebook recalculates verification and figures
from saved results. Case two executes four PyCPT fits and requires the full fitting
environment. The table separates these activities.

| Activity | Required setup | PyCPT / CPT / IRIDL credentials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read the executed notebook | Browser | None |
| Run the default saved-results cells | Scientific Python, Jupyter and the complete kit | None |
| Optional OND model refit | Tested PyCPT environment with its CPT engine and the supplied inputs | PyCPT and CPT required; no IRIDL credentials |
| Execute case-two OND/JJA fitting notebook | Full tested PyCPT environment and complete fitting kit | PyCPT and CPT required; no IRIDL credentials |
| Download new data in an extended workflow | Network access and permissions for the chosen source | Authentication only when the dataset requires it |

## Case one: run the saved-results notebook {#offline-analysis}

Download and extract the [complete tutorial kit](../downloads/indonesia-seasons-2023-kit.zip).
It includes the executed notebook, five national NetCDF inputs, four regional
NetCDF inputs, display boundaries, helper code and environment specifications.
The notebook file alone does not include those inputs and helpers.

**Mandatory:** Python with NumPy, pandas, xarray, Matplotlib, netCDF4 and
Jupyter/IPython, plus a writable copy of the kit or repository.
**Helpful:** basic Python/Jupyter familiarity. **Not required:** PyCPT, a CPT
executable, Quarto or an IRI Data Library key.

From the extracted kit or repository root, create a separate analysis environment:

```bash
conda env create -f environment/offline-analysis.yml
conda activate pycpt-tutorial-analysis
python -m ipykernel install --user --name pycpt-tutorial-analysis --display-name "Python (Tutorial Analysis)"
jupyter notebook docs/notebooks/indonesia-seasons-2023.ipynb
```

Select **Python (Tutorial Analysis)** and run the cells from top to bottom with
`RERUN_CPT = False`. The [analysis environment file](../downloads/offline-analysis.yml)
lists direct package versions used by the verified runtime; it contains no PyCPT
or CPT dependency. It is a requirements specification, not a full cross-platform lock.
If you already have a working tutorial environment, you can use it for this step.
Initial package installation can require internet access; execution afterward uses
the supplied local inputs and does not download data or fit models.

The notebook checks input hashes, recalculates scores, and writes derived figures,
tables and NetCDF outputs under `docs/assets/seasonal-2023/`. It also writes story
findings under `docs/_includes/`. Run it in your own extracted kit or checkout.
The original preparation drives are not needed for this workflow.

::: {.callout-tip title="Verified in a fresh analysis-only environment"}
On 2 November 2026, this complete kit was tested in a new conda environment on
Debian under WSL2 (Linux x86-64), created from the analysis environment file above.
All **22 original code cells** completed with PyCPT/CPT packages absent and no
credential reads, remote connections or CPT launches. The three generated NetCDF
files and eleven CSV tables matched the saved results within numerical tolerances;
the findings and generated story text matched exactly. All nine PNG figures were
generated successfully. The test ran a kit copy and preserved the published notebook.

This verifies the default saved-results workflow on that platform. Package
installation used internet access; notebook execution used local inputs.
Other operating systems have not been tested with this smaller specification.
:::

## Prepare the full PyCPT fitting environment {#use-the-tested-debian-environment}

PyCPT is the Python interface used to fit CCA and PCR in this case. Its calibration
functions rely on a compatible CPT executable. Use the supplied environment
specification so the Python packages and CPT engine are provided together; a manual
CPT source build is not part of this tutorial.
This environment is required to execute case two and optional for the case-one refit.

The tested fitting environment uses **PyCPT 2.10.4, cptio 1.4.0 and CPT 17.8.3**.
Its explicit lock targets the verified Linux x86-64 runtime. From a conda installation:

```bash
conda create -n pycpt-tutorial --file environment/conda-linux-64.lock
conda activate pycpt-tutorial
python -m ipykernel install --user --name pycpt-tutorial --display-name "Python (PyCPT Tutorial)"
jupyter notebook docs/notebooks/indonesia-seasons-2023.ipynb
```

Activation selects the packaged CPT engine through `CPT_BIN_DIR`. These instructions
describe the setup used to verify this fitting workflow. For platform-specific
PyCPT environment instructions, consult the [upstream installation guide](https://iri-pycpt.github.io/installation/).

## Optional: fit OND again

In **Python (PyCPT Tutorial)**, set `RERUN_CPT = True` only in the optional notebook
cell. PyCPT fits CCA and PCR using the supplied local OND inputs, records commands
and logs in a unique scratch directory, checks deterministic forecasts against the
saved case, and exports the new forecasts as NetCDF. It refits OND only and preserves
the frozen research archive. No IRIDL authentication is needed for these local inputs.

## Case two: execute the fitting notebook {#fitting-case-setup}

Download and extract the [complete fitting kit](../downloads/fit-diagnose-2023-kit.zip).
It contains the executed notebook, prepared OND/JJA training and 2023 inputs,
frozen control forecasts/diagnostics, country/province/display boundaries, helper
code and the tested Linux environment lock. The notebook alone is insufficient.

**Mandatory for execution:** the full PyCPT fitting environment described above,
the complete kit and a writable working folder. The analysis-only environment
does not execute these fitting cells. Reading the executed pages needs only a browser.

From the extracted fitting kit or repository root, using the full environment:

```bash
conda activate pycpt-tutorial
python -m ipykernel install --user --name pycpt-tutorial --display-name "Python (PyCPT Tutorial)"
jupyter notebook docs/notebooks/fit-diagnose-2023.ipynb
```

Choose **Python (PyCPT Tutorial)** and run all cells. There is no fitting switch:
this notebook deliberately makes four actual calibration calls. Each execution
creates a new scratch folder under `temp/`, checks the engine and wrapper identity,
and compares the new results with the controls. Local inputs mean no IRIDL key
or new source download is required. Never put credentials in the notebook or kit.

The notebook saves 30 NetCDF files, tables, figures and an execution manifest
under `docs/assets/fitting-2023/`. It retains all datasets returned by CCA/PCR,
plus cleaned diagnostics with explicit mode axes and derived correlation maps.
The fitting inputs and frozen controls are hash-checked and preserved.
The conda release is PyCPT 2.10.4; the tested package's Python metadata reports
`2.10.4.dev0`. Both identifiers and the checked engine/wrapper hashes are recorded.

- [Executed fitting notebook](../downloads/fit-diagnose-2023.ipynb)
- [Complete fitting kit](../downloads/fit-diagnose-2023-kit.zip)
- [All fitted NetCDF outputs and provenance](../downloads/fit-diagnose-2023-outputs.zip)
- [Execution manifest](../assets/fitting-2023/execution-manifest.json)
- [Variable-specific control checks](../assets/fitting-2023/control-checks.csv)

Other platforms have not been verified for this fitting case. Rendering Quarto
uses the saved outputs and does not execute the fitting calls.

::: {.callout-tip title="The complete fitting kit was executed separately"}
The distributed kit was extracted to a new directory and all 18 code cells ran,
including four actual fits. All 30 NetCDF datasets matched the canonical outputs
exactly, the five CSV tables matched, and all six PNG figures were byte-identical.
The interactive values and generated story findings also matched. The run used
the tested full fitting environment with no credential reads or remote connections.
:::

## Optional: authenticate for protected downloads

None of the local-input workflows above downloads new inputs. Authentication becomes relevant
only when extending the workflow to a protected IRI Data Library dataset. The
[official authentication guide](https://iri-pycpt.github.io/authentication/)
explains that most datasets are public and protected datasets require authorization.
The requirement depends on the dataset, rather than on a seasonal/S2S label alone.
Keep credentials outside notebooks and repositories; do not add a key to this tutorial.

## Optional: rebuild the website

Quarto is needed only to render the website, not to read the published pages or
execute the notebook. From the full repository with Quarto installed:

```bash
python scripts/render_tutorial.py
```

The tested renderer is Quarto 1.8.27. This uses saved, already-executed notebook
outputs without executing cells, downloading data or fitting models. Use a local
HTTP preview, such as `quarto preview docs`, for the interactive story.
